name: TES x-ray microcalorimeter (Lynx LXM ultra-high-resolution array) characterization at a 42-50 mK ADR bath with magnetic shielding and microwave-SQUID/HEMT readout
plain_name: Test an X-ray detector that measures the energy of single X-ray photons as a tiny temperature rise
description: Transition-edge-sensor x-ray microcalorimeter arrays for the Lynx X-ray Microcalorimeter are characterized (R-T, pulses, energy resolution with Al/Mn K-alpha) on a sub-100 mK bath: a 4.5 K cryocooler stage plus a multistage ADR to ~50 mK; the first UHR array, with Tc ~10 mK below the 65 mK target, had to be run at a 42 mK bath. TESs require careful magnetic shielding, and multiplexed readout uses microwave SQUID resonators with a 4-8 GHz HEMT at ~4 K.
keywords: Test an X-ray detector that measures the energy of single X-ray photons as a tiny temperature rise

sources.citation: S. R. Bandler, J. A. Chervenak, A. M. Datesman et al., 'Lynx x-ray microcalorimeter', J. Astron. Telesc. Instrum. Syst. 5(2), 021017 (2019), doi:10.1117/1.JATIS.5.2.021017 (PMC7802767)

reported_equipment: Low Noise Factory LNF-LNC4_8DRPA 4-8 GHz cryogenic LNA

requirements.rationale: The UHR array had to be characterized at a 42 mK bath temperature (nominal 50 mK).
TES microcalorimeters are sensitive to magnetic fields; the focal plane needs magnetic shielding.
TES bias and SQUID readout lines must reach the array.
Optional: the microwave SQUID multiplexer is amplified by a 4-8 GHz HEMT at ~4 K, so coax lines rated to 8 GHz are needed for this readout (a DC-SQUID TDM readout would not need them).
Optional: the nominal operating bath is 50 mK, provided by an ADR below a 4.5 K cryocooler stage.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
